meaning: to understand a hidden meaning that is not stated directly
literal_translation: captar el significado oculto de lo que no se dice explícitamente
example: The email said we would review our work soon, so I read between the lines and knew the news was bad.
origin: Comes from the idea of finding a message hidden in the spaces between the printed lines of a text

wrong_meanings.meaning: to read very slowly, one line at a time
wrong_meanings.why_wrong: This describes a reading speed, not understanding a hidden meaning

wrong_meanings.meaning: to skip parts of a book
wrong_meanings.why_wrong: The idiom is about understanding, not about leaving out text

wrong_meanings.meaning: to write notes in the margins of a page
wrong_meanings.why_wrong: This is a physical action; the idiom describes a mental interpretation

explanation: 'Read between the lines' means to understand what someone really means when they do not say it directly. It is often used with emails, messages and news.
